name: AerialBomb
label: Aerial bomb explosion
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: transparent top-down explosion sprite sheet.
Input image 1 is the edit target. Preserve its realistic painted explosion/fire/smoke artwork style and sixteen-frame ignition, expansion, cooling smoke, full fade chronology.
Fix ONLY the sprite layout and clearance. Re-render the animation as an EXACTLY SQUARE canvas with an EXACT 4-by-4 grid of equal square cells. There are 16 frames, row-major, fixed impact pivot at each cell center. No labels or visible grid.
Every sprite MUST fit within the CENTRAL 50 PERCENT of the cell width AND height, leaving an enormous empty transparent margin on every side of each cell. Even the largest smoke billow or spark cannot exceed this central half-cell region. This large clearance is essential for slicing the animation into individual sprites. All sprites centered identically. No shifted smoke, no neighboring frame intrusion, no objects touching a cell boundary or canvas edge.
Make the very first frame a small flash, grow the fire and dust in frames 2-6, cool fire into smoke in frames 7-11, progressively fade thin smoke in frames 12-15, and leave the LAST CELL ENTIRELY EMPTY TRANSPARENT.
Subject remains a conventional aerial bomb explosion with hot orange fireball, brown-grey dust shockwave and charcoal smoke.
Preserve the strict vertical overhead camera; never a side-view cloud. Maintain coherent principal smoke lobes over time. Genuine alpha around every frame and through faint smoke. No ground disk, painted backdrop, crater, text, border or watermark.
Most important: massive consistent transparent padding INSIDE EVERY CELL; exactly square whole sheet, 4 equal columns and 4 equal rows. No artwork crosses a cell boundary.

previousGenerations.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: animated strategy-game VFX sprite atlas for Age of Fronts, transparent PNG.
Primary request: draw a genuinely coherent single explosion evolving in time across EXACTLY SIXTEEN frames. This is a 4-column by 4-row sprite sheet, sixteen equally sized square cells, read left-to-right then next row.
Composition: uniform 4 x 4 grid with no visible grid lines, no text, no gutters and no outer decorative border. Every square cell has a perfectly centered impact at its cell center. All sixteen frames use identical camera, light, scale reference and center. Keep each effect completely inside its cell with wide transparent clearance. No particles or smoke may enter a neighbouring cell.
Camera: perfectly vertical 90-degree TOP DOWN orthographic ground-impact view. We see the upper surfaces of radial fire, dust and smoke. No side-view mushroom cloud, horizon, oblique view or isometric perspective.
Style: realistic richly textured hand-painted strategy-game effects, natural orange/yellow fire with hot pale center, turbulent dark grey smoke, brown-grey dust, fine sparks and irregular wispy edges. Polished matching the existing realistic textured building and bomb icon set. The artwork must remain clear at small game-map scale.
Animation continuity: one and the same impact expands radially, burns briefly, cools to smoke and fades away. Preserve the principal smoke lobes and particle paths progressively across adjacent frames; do not redraw sixteen unrelated explosions. No cut to a different shot, no camera movement, no late second flash.
Timing/storyboard, row-major:
1 tiny pale ignition flash; 2 brighter compact flash; 3 small expanding orange fireball; 4 larger fiery burst.
5 fireball grows and first radial dust ring; 6 peak orange flame and sparks; 7 flames start cooling into smoky lobes; 8 smoke expands while fire dims.
9 faint central embers under smoke; 10 expanding dust and dark smoke; 11 diffuse grey smoke with almost no flame; 12 softer thinner smoke.
13 low-opacity cooling smoke; 14 wispy fading remnants; 15 barely visible dispersed smoke; 16 completely empty transparent cell.
Outside every individual effect, preserve TRUE TRANSPARENT ALPHA including through faint smoke and glow. No painted black/white/checkerboard background, ground tile, persistent crater, buildings, aircraft, physical bomb, human, label, border or watermark.
Subject: a conventional aerial bomb ground explosion. A forceful broad irregular radial orange fireball with a small brilliant yellow center, scattered tiny sparks, a rapidly expanding uneven dusty shockwave, then thick charcoal-grey smoke cooling and dissipating. Peak effect occupies about 82 percent of its cell width. Finite one-shot detonation, not continuous burning or a repeating campfire.
